en.title: Grid Shortest Path Where Long Jumps Lock the Direction
en.description:
The grid contains empty cells *, walls #, a start S, and an end E. Each move jumps a positive integer distance up, down, left, or right; a jump may pass over walls but cannot land on a wall. If the previous jump had length >1, the next jump must go in the same direction; a jump of length 1 lifts the restriction. E counts as reached only when the last move has length 1 and lands on E. If E cannot be reached, output −1.

The input/output protocol was compiled independently by this site; upstream solutions are not executed.
en.input: The first line contains n m, followed by n lines of the grid; 2≤n,m≤100, and there is exactly one S and exactly one E.
en.output: Output the single integer required by the problem.
en.explanation: The answers to the three public examples are, in order: 1; 4; -1. All examples have been verified by independent small-scale enumeration or state search.
hints: Run BFS on states made of the coordinates and the locked direction (plus a free state), enumerating the allowed directions and all valid landing cells; a long jump locks the direction, and a short jump makes the state free.
